description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:209-213 (Error::Aia rustdoc): 'Carries the underlying pkix_aia::AiaError from the last fetch attempt; earlier failures are dropped because the chain builder iterates URIs in caller-supplied order and only the final blocker determines the outcome.' This is misleading. Looking at build_with_aia (lines 620-668): the iteration order is (1) by orphan cert in pool.iter(), (2) by URI from ca_issuers_http_uris (which is in AIA-extension order on each cert), (3) skipping URIs already in tried_uris. The 'final' URI's error has no special significance — it's just whichever URI happened to be processed last in iteration N's batch. If iteration 0 fetches 3 URIs and iteration 1 fetches 2, the 'last AIA error' surfaced may be from iter 1 even though iter 0 had the actual relevant fetches. Reword to: 'Carries the most-recent AiaError surfaced during fetch iterations. The order in which URIs were attempted is implementation-defined (currently: iteration-major, then orphan-cert-major within each iteration, then AIA-extension order within each cert).'
title: AIA last_aia_error rustdoc misrepresents URI ordering
